issues.legal_issue: A tenant is entitled to leave to contest a summary eviction proceeding when the tenant raises prima facie grounds which, if accepted, could defeat the landlord’s claim to eviction.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the basis of a claimed inheritance through adoption and produced an adoption deed said to have been executed many years earlier.
The tenant disputed the claimant’s ownership and landlord status, had not attorned to the claimant, and challenged whether a landlord-tenant relationship existed between them.
The tenant specifically alleged that alternative accommodation in the building was available to meet the claimed need for the premises.
The lower authorities refused leave without allowing the tenant to contest the eviction claim on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had raised prima facie grounds sufficient to obtain leave to contest. The refusal of leave was set aside and the eviction proceeding was restored for decision on its merits. Leave was subject to depositing the rent arrears and continuing to deposit rent; failure to comply would result in refusal to contest.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 25B(4) and 25B(5) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, the authority considering leave to contest should not determine the merits and demerits of the proposed defences. Leave is warranted where the grounds prima facie disclose a defence which, if accepted, may disentitle the landlord to eviction. The eviction claim in this case was brought under Section 14(1)(e). The Court cited no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: summary_rent_eviction_leave_application and ownership_or_landlord_status_disputed and tenancy_relationship_unproven and alternative_accommodation_specifically_pleaded

predicates.summary_rent_eviction_leave_application: A tenant applied for leave to contest a proceeding in which a landlord sought eviction under a summary rent-control procedure.
predicates.ownership_or_landlord_status_disputed: The tenant disputed the claimant’s ownership of the premises or status as landlord, including by challenging the basis on which that status was claimed.
predicates.tenancy_relationship_unproven: The tenant disputed the existence of a landlord-tenant relationship, and the record did not establish that relationship between the tenant and the claimant.
predicates.alternative_accommodation_specifically_p: The tenant specifically alleged that other suitable accommodation was available to meet the claimant’s stated need.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks leave in a summary rent-eviction proceeding and disputes the claimant’s ownership or landlord status and the tenancy relationship while specifically pleading available alternative accommodation, the tenant is granted leave subject to compliance with rent-payment conditions.
